questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes a program audit from a workplace inspection?
options: An audit is always unannounced while an inspection is always scheduled
An audit evaluates the management system and its effectiveness; an inspection focuses on conditions and practices
An inspection can review documents but an audit cannot
The terms are identical and require the same evidence
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Audits test whether the system is designed, implemented, and effective; inspections more directly identify current workplace conditions.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Scheduling does not define whether an activity is an audit or inspection.
Inspections may include records, and audits commonly rely heavily on documents and interviews.
The activities may overlap but have different scope and objectives.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 37, purpose and methodology of auditing, pp. 818-825

questions.stem: A department manager selects evidence and removes two adverse findings before the audit report is issued. Which audit principle is most threatened?
options: Sampling precision only
Training transfer only
Objectivity and independence
Equipment reliability only
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Auditors need freedom to evaluate and report evidence without inappropriate influence from the function being audited.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Sampling may be affected, but management suppression primarily compromises impartial reporting.
The scenario concerns audit governance, not training application.
No equipment reliability evidence is described.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 37, audit methodology, documentation, and interviews, pp. 818-843

questions.stem: A procedure states that weekly inspections occur, but employees describe monthly inspections and records show long gaps. What should the auditor conclude?
options: The written procedure alone proves conformity
Employee interviews should always override records
No conclusion is possible unless an injury occurred
The documented procedure is not reliably implemented and the conflicting evidence requires a finding
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Triangulating documents, interviews, records, and observations tests both system design and actual implementation.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A document describes intent; implementation requires corroborating evidence.
Interviews are one evidence source and should be weighed with records and observations.
Audit findings are based on criteria and evidence, not on waiting for harm.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 37, documentation, employee interviews, and site conditions, pp. 818-843

questions.stem: A multisite audit examines only one high-performing location selected by management. What is the primary weakness?
options: The sample is unlikely to represent the organization and may bias the conclusion
Every audit must inspect every record and location
High-performing sites cannot provide any useful evidence
Sampling is prohibited in management-system audits
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Risk-based and representative sampling reduces selection bias and supports a defensible conclusion within the stated scope.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Audits commonly sample, but the sample must be appropriate to objectives and risk.
Strong sites can provide evidence, but they should not be the only management-selected sample.
Sampling is a normal audit technique when limitations are understood.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 37, audit methodology and worksite analysis, pp. 818-839

questions.stem: An audit finds that required emergency drills were not performed at three facilities. What makes the finding defensible?
options: Describe the auditor personal opinion only
State the criterion, objective evidence, scope, and resulting nonconformity clearly
Name the lowest-level employee responsible without evidence
Use vague wording so management can interpret it later
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A strong finding connects an applicable criterion to specific evidence and explains the gap without unsupported blame.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A personal opinion is not a traceable audit basis.
Accountability should follow evidence and system ownership, not scapegoating.
Vague findings are difficult to correct, verify, and close.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 37, audit documentation and assessment of program elements, pp. 818-843

questions.stem: An audit finding is closed after a memo is issued, but the same failure recurs. What was most likely missing?
options: A longer memo
A lower audit score
Root-cause correction and verification that the action was effective
A new name for the finding
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Closure should require action on causes and evidence that the change is implemented and sustained.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Length does not demonstrate that causes were removed.
Changing the score does not change the underlying process.
Renaming a finding does not prevent recurrence.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 37, program effectiveness and root causes, pp. 820-857

questions.stem: Before fieldwork begins, which audit element should be agreed and documented?
options: The desired final score
The employees who will be disciplined
A promise that no findings will be issued
Objectives, criteria, scope, methods, timing, and responsibilities
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Clear scope and criteria establish what will be evaluated, against what requirements, and how the audit will be conducted.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Predetermining a score compromises the evidence-based process.
An audit identifies system gaps and should not begin as a disciplinary exercise.
Guaranteeing no findings destroys audit credibility.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 37, purpose and methodology for conducting audits, pp. 818-825

questions.stem: What is a common advantage of an external audit team?
options: Greater independence and a fresh comparison against external practice
Guaranteed knowledge of every local process detail
Automatic legal privilege for all findings
Elimination of the need for internal audits
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: External reviewers can add objectivity and broader experience, while internal teams often add local knowledge and continuity.
incorrectOptionExplanations: External auditors often require orientation to local operations.
Legal privilege depends on jurisdiction and engagement structure, not simply auditor status.
Internal monitoring remains important between external reviews.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 37 and homework, internal and external audit advantages and limitations

questions.stem: Which evidence best supports closing a corrective action for missing machine-guard inspections?
options: A purchase order for inspection software
Completed inspections over a sustained period plus verification that the scheduling failure was corrected
A manager verbal promise
A revised due date with no completed work
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Closure should show both implementation and effectiveness, including evidence that the causal process failure has been addressed.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A purchase can support action but does not prove the process is working.
A promise is not objective implementation or effectiveness evidence.
Rescheduling does not correct or verify the gap.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 37, assessing effectiveness and program controls, pp. 832-857

questions.stem: Three audits show repeated findings in contractor orientation across different sites. What is the best management response?
options: Close each finding independently with no cross-site review
Stop auditing contractor orientation
Treat it as a systemic weakness and address the common process and governance
Lower the significance of future findings because they are common
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Cross-audit analysis can identify organizational patterns that require enterprise-level ownership, standards, resources, and verification.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Independent closure can miss the shared system cause.
Stopping review hides the weakness and removes assurance.
Frequency increases the evidence of a systemic issue; it does not reduce significance.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 37, trend analysis and assessing overall program effectiveness, pp. 829-857
